name: Getting Started
description_html:
Welcome to Your Project

This guide will help you get up and running quickly.

Quick Setup

  1. Clone the repository
  2. Install dependencies with bun install
  3. Copy .env.example to .env
  4. Run bun dev to start the development server

Project Structure

The codebase is organized into modules for easy navigation. Refer to the Architecture page for more details.

children.name: Environment Setup
children.description_html:
Environment Setup

Required tools and configuration for local development.

  • Bun v1.0+ — JavaScript runtime
  • SQLite — Database engine
  • Git — Version control

Run bun install in the project root to install all dependencies.

children.name: Deployment Guide
children.description_html:
Deployment

Steps to deploy the application to production.

  1. Build the project: bun run build
  2. Run database migrations
  3. Set environment variables
  4. Start the server: bun start

name: Architecture Overview
description_html:
Architecture Overview

This project follows a layered architecture pattern with clear separation of concerns.

Backend

  • Routes — HTTP endpoint definitions using Hono
  • Middleware — Authentication, authorization, and validation
  • Database — Drizzle ORM with SQLite
  • Schema — Type-safe table definitions

Frontend

  • Components — React components with MobX state management
  • Services — API client layer
  • Stores — MobX observable stores

name: API Reference
description_html:

All endpoints follow RESTful conventions and return JSON responses.

name: Research — Real-time Collaboration
description_html:
Real-time Collaboration Research

Investigation into approaches for real-time collaborative editing.

Options Evaluated

  1. Y.js (CRDT) — Conflict-free replicated data type. Excellent offline support, mature library.
  2. Operational Transformation — Used by Google Docs. Complex to implement correctly.
  3. Automerge — Another CRDT library, Rust-based. Good performance.

Recommendation

Y.js is the recommended approach. It has the best ecosystem support, works well with popular editors (TipTap, ProseMirror), and handles offline/merge scenarios gracefully.

Next Steps

  • Prototype Y.js integration with TipTap editor
  • Load test with 10+ concurrent editors
  • Evaluate WebSocket vs WebRTC for transport
